3472.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ergʰ- (“to mount”), whence also perhaps Hittite [script needed] (arkatta, “to mount sexually”).

3463.t: Verbal abstract from ἰδεῖν (ĭdeîn, aor. of ὁράω (horắō)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyd- (“to see”). Closely related to εἶδος (eîdos).

3465.t: From ἱστορέω (hĭstoréō, “to inquire”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from ἵστωρ (hístōr, “one who knows, wise one”).

3489.t: Likely borrowed from unattested Phoenician *𐤊𐤓𐤊-𐤇𐤃𐤔𐤕 (*krk-ḥdšt, “new city”) (cf. Aramaic כַּרְכָא, Hebrew כְּרַךְ), variant of 𐤒𐤓𐤕-𐤇𐤃𐤔𐤕 (qrt-ḥdšt), hence doublet of Χαλκηδών (Khalkēdṓn, “Chalcedon”).

3492.t: Perhaps originally “entangler” or “binder”, from σειρά (seirā́, “rope; cord”), from Proto-Indo-European *twerH- (“to grab; to seize; to enclose”).

3466.t: From Proto-Hellenic *yīyēmi, reduplicated present of Proto-Indo-European *(H)yeh₁- (“to throw”). Compare Latin iaciō, Hittite [script needed] (pe-iezzi, “sends away”).

3481.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *ōyyón, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”), argued to have been a derivative of *h₂éwis (“bird”), whence also ἀετός (āetós, “eagle”) and οἰωνός (oiōnós, “bird of prey”).

3497.t: From αὐτο- (auto-, “self”) + Proto-Hellenic *mətós, from Proto-Indo-European *mn̥tós, from *men- (“to think”) (whence μένος (ménos) and others).

3402.t: It has been proposed to derive from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʷs-ih₂-, citing cognates such as Latin ascia and a number of Germanic words, such as Old English æx (English axe).

3459.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hédrā, from Proto-Indo-European *sedreh₂, from *sed- (“to sit”) (whence ἕζομαι (hézomai, “I sit”) and many others).

3462.t: From older *ϝήθος (*wḗthos), an expanded form of ἔθος (éthos). Cognate with Sanskrit स्व॒धा (svadhā́, “habit; custom”).

3410.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂erǵ- Proto-Indo-European *-rós Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥ǵrós Ancient Greek *ἀργρός (*ărgrós) Ancient Greek ἀργός Dissimilated from an earlier *ἀργρός (*argrós), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂r̥ǵ-ró-s, from *h₂erǵ-…

3439.t: From ἐπαγγέλλω (epangéllō, “to announce, promise”) (from ἐπι- (epi-, “on”) + ἀγγέλλω (angéllō, “to announce”)) + -ία (-íā). Compare typologically Latin prōmissum, Russian по́сул (pósul) (? akin to слать (slatʹ)).

3432.t: From ἐνεργός (energós, “active, effective”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix).

3449.t: From ἐπι- (epĭ-, “upon”) + γνῶσις (gnôsĭs, “inquiry, knowledge”), or from ἐπιγιγνώσκω (epĭgĭgnṓskō) + -σις (-sĭs).

3498.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂emǵʰ-w-eh₁-n, from *h₂énǵʰus (“narrow, tight”), and compared in particular to Old Armenian օձիք (ōjikʻ, “collar”), though this is controversial.

3499.t: Compared with Lithuanian vilkti (“to drag, haul”) and Proto-Slavic *velťi (“to draw”). Beekes claims that the variants point to a Pre-Greek origin, in particular a form *alʷ-ak-.

3484.t: Perhaps related to ῥέω (rhéō, “to flow”), because of the richness of the juice, with hypothetical original form *ῥοϝ-ιά (*rhow-iá). However, a Pre-Greek origin remains a serious option for this word.

3482.t: From the root of ῥαίνω (rhaínō, “to sprinkle”) + -τός (-tós).

3485.t: From Aramaic גַמַלִיאיֵל (Ḡamalīʾēl) from Biblical Hebrew גַּמְלִיאֵל (Gamlīʾēl). Compare Classical Syriac ܓ݂ܰܡܰܠܺܝܐܝܶܠ (Ḡamalīʾēl).

3425.t: From ἐκ- (ek-, “out, away, off”) + λάμπω (lắmpō, “to give light, shine”).

3434.t: From ἐν- (en-, “in-”) + νοέω (noéō, “to perceive, think, deem”).
